newsitem.title: UK: DuPont to pick up 50 pct in ICI Pak.
newsitem.headline: DuPont to pick up 50 pct in ICI Pak.

text.p: British chemicals giant ICI Plc said on Monday that U.S. group DuPont will pick up a 50 percent stake in one of its subsidiaries ICI Pakistan Ltd.
ICI said the deal was part of an agreement to sell most of its bulk chemical business to DuPont for $3 billion, details of which were announced earlier on Monday.
"We also intend that ICI Pakistan should set up a new joint venture with DuPont a 50 percent share in the PTA plant in Pakistan," ICI's chief executive Charles Miller Smith told a news conference.
ICI Pakistan, listed on the Karachi Stock Exchange, is currently owned 61 percent by ICI. It manufactures polyester staple fibre, soda ash, paints and other speciality chemicals.
ICI's effective exposure to the Pakistan business will be reduced to about 30 percent, he said.
ICI is also selling its PTA plants in the UK and its 70 percent shareholding in its PTA plants in Taiwan.

Smith said DuPont has also agreed to reimburse for up to $100 million of the relevant proportion of capital expenditure to be incurred by ICI on the plants currently under construction in Taiwan and Pakistan prior to the completion of the proposals.
